verdict.reasoning: Patient describes diarrhoea as “just coming out, like loads of it… super watery… just pouring straight from my bum,” indicating profuse watery diarrhea.

Onset: “it was about three, it's been about three days now.” Frequency: “I feel like it's like almost every hour, when I'm awake.” Description: “it's like basically I think it's diarrhoea… super watery.”

Location: “it's like at the bottom… it feels pretty like in the middle, to me.” Nature and timing: “I feel, I feel a cramp… and then I know it's time to go… it comes and goes.” Severity: patient suggests “maybe is that like a six, or a seven?” and doctor repeats “solid six.”

Patient states: “yeah I definitely feel kind of nauseous… I've have vomited… whenever I have like milk… I just feel like I want to vomit. And actually, yeah one time I just like had some milk, and I just completely vomited it.”

Patient reports: “I think I am pretty, I feel kind of really hot all the time… I'm pretty sure I'm burning up… I haven't actually done any temperature reading,” indicating subjective fever without measured temperature.
When asked about blood: “Have you got any blood in your stools?” Patient replies: “no I don't… I think it's just… nothing like that. There's nothing like that.”
Doctor: “are you passing urine OK?” Patient: “yeah a bit, I guess less frequently maybe. Um but yeah, it seems to be OK.” This supports decreased urine frequency.
Fluids: “the fluids do go down. But it just feels like it's going straight through.” Food: “I had some lunch today… but again it just it just came, come out pretty loose.”
Patient: “my brother has had, actually had something like this for… he has it as well for five days… I think he's getting better, but I'm not really sure.”

When asked about other medical history: patient says, “yeah I think, I think otherwise I'm fit and well… I can't think of any related medical history… no I I don't think so,” indicating no past medical history reported.

Doctor: “I'll take it you don't take any regular medications, then.” Patient: “No I mean I, I've been taking some like Paracetamols and stuff like that lately. But… I'm not on any regular medication.” This indicates PRN Paracetamol use.
Doctor: “do you have any allergies to any medications?” Patient: “I don't have any allergies that I know of.”
Patient: “my dad actually has um colon cancer at the moment… he's sort of in his third stage.” This corresponds to colon cancer reported as stage 3.
Patient: “I live with my, um sister and my mum.”
Patient: “I work at um an office, um in Central London. Um it's uh, so I work in government.”
Patient: “I smoke… for like socially, but not like regularly… if it's a, a Friday or something like that I might have a cigarette,” indicating social smoking.

Alcohol: “I might have a a beer during the weekdays… On Fridays I have more alcohol… not every week, but maybe I'll once or twice a month… I'll go out with my friends and drink a lot,” matching beers on weekdays and heavier drinking 1–2 times per month.
Impact on work: “it's been tricky… Going to work with all of this. Um I dislike taking time off work. I feel like I just want to go,” showing current symptoms are impacting work.

Doctor states: “your symptoms are suggestive of something called gastroenteritis.” History includes: 3 days (“about three days now”) of watery diarrhea nearly hourly, intermittent crampy lower mid-abdominal pain (“bottom… in the middle… comes and goes”), nausea/vomiting with milk, subjective fever (“burning up”), contact with brother with similar illness, and no blood in stool (“nothing like that”). All components are in the transcript.

Doctor: “you're losing a lot of fluid… I am obviously worried about the fact that you are losing minerals and vitamins… if you are getting dehydrated then we need to do further investigations.” Patient also notes very frequent watery stools and “less frequently maybe” passing urine, supporting dehydration risk.

Doctor: “Drink, make sure you drink plenty of fluids… you can get things like Diarolyte, which is um, a fluid replacement you can get from the pharmacy… no, you can just get that over the counter.” This matches oral rehydration solution and clear fluids.
Doctor: “clear fluids. You can use soft diet, things like soup, mash. And then gradually build up, um as much as your body can tolerate.”

Doctor: “you can try just you know regular Paracetamol if you are feeling feverish.” Later: “If you are having, if you've got a bit of tummy pain, if you're feeling feverish, then I think Paracetamol is very sensible.”
Doctor advises: “Try and avoid alcohol if you can.”

Doctor: “if your symptoms aren't settling down in the next couple of days, so forty eight hours, I want you to give me a call back… if you are getting dehydrated then we need to do further investigations.” This aligns with follow-up for lack of improvement in 48 hours or dehydration/red flags.
